newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals futures slip on firm yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals futures slip on firm yen.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metals futures ended lower across the board on Thursday, weighed down by the yen's firmer tone against the dollar, traders said on Thursday.
Gold prices ranged from four to six yen per gram lower, with benchmark October ending down six yen at 1,325 yen.
Activity was mainly dominated by trade houses' inter-month trade, with limited participation of private investors, the traders said.
Bullion was quoted at $369.00/369.30 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $368.60/369.10 in New York on Wednesday.

In the gold bullion market, spot gold was sandwiched between looming Australian producer selling above $369 and Swiss investors' bidding at around $368.80 during Asian hours. Market participants were divided over near-term direction.
"The bullion market lacked momentum despite a fall in the U.S. stock market," one trading house trader said.
Another trader said the market may rebound slightly on short-covering by investment funds.
Platinum futures ranged from four to seven yen per gram lower, with benchmark October contract ending down six yen at 1,334 yen.
Palladium futures were relatively steady as constant bargain hunting buying was offset by the yen's firmer tone.
In the spot Tokyo market, palladium was quoted at around $1.5 per ounce over the world benchmark, compared with flat or a slight discount in early October.
Delayed Japan-Russia platinum talks for 1997 were partly responsible to the firmer spot prices, they said.
Benchmark October silver futures ended 0.4 yen per 10 grams lower at 177.7 yen. Benchmark October palladium futures ended two yen per gram down at 429 yen.
